subject: Chemistry
title: The Montreal Protocol: Chemistry's Greatest Save
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Montreal Protocol: Chemistry's Greatest Save.

hook.text: The Montreal Protocol is the only UN treaty ratified by every country on Earth. It saved the ozone layer from destruction.

buildup.text: After discovering the ozone hole in 1985, nations agreed within two years to phase out CFCs and related chemicals.

discovery.text: CFC production dropped 99% by 2010. The ozone layer stopped thinning and began recovering measurably.

twist.text: The Protocol also prevented 2°C of extra global warming. CFCs are potent greenhouse gases—thousands of times worse than CO₂.

climax.text: Scientists estimate the Protocol will prevent 443 million skin cancer cases and 2.3 million skin cancer deaths by 2100.

punchline.text: Every nation agreed, one chemical class banned. Chemistry disasters can be reversed.

quiz.question: Besides saving the ozone layer, what other benefit did the Montreal Protocol provide?
options: It prevented about 2°C of additional global warming since CFCs are potent greenhouse gases
It eliminated acid rain in the Northern Hemisphere
It cleaned up all existing CFC contamination in the atmosphere

details.summary: The 1987 Montreal Protocol is an international treaty that phased out the production and use of ozone-depleting substances including CFCs and halons. Ratified by every United Nations member state, it is the most universally adopted environmental agreement and has prevented catastrophic ozone loss.
details.whyItMatters: The Montreal Protocol proved that global chemical regulation can work when science, industry, and governments align. It prevented an estimated two million skin cancer cases annually by 2030.
takeaways: It is the only UN treaty ratified by all 198 member states
CFC production dropped over 99% following the protocol
The Kigali Amendment extended it to cover climate-warming HFCs

faq.question: How did the Montreal Protocol achieve universal ratification?
faq.answer: The combination of clear scientific evidence, industry willingness to develop alternatives, and a funding mechanism for developing countries made adoption feasible. DuPont's early support for alternatives removed industrial opposition, and financial aid addressed equity concerns.

faq.question: What is the Kigali Amendment and why was it added?
faq.answer: The 2016 Kigali Amendment extended the Montreal Protocol to phase down hydrofluorocarbons, which replaced CFCs but are potent greenhouse gases. While HFCs do not harm ozone, they contribute to global warming thousands of times more than CO2 per molecule.
